title: 第五章 无言的军舰第六章 擦臂而过的兵
lines: 第五章：无言的军舰
凌峰扶着刘佳琪的胳膊，两人沿着山腰的碎石路慢慢往下走。山顶那道刺目的白光已经消失，只留下空气中一丝若有若无的灼热感，像是刚熄灭的炭火余温。风从耳边掠过，带着山林里潮湿的草木气息，可这熟悉的自然味道，却压不住心底翻涌的慌乱。
“佳琪，你还好吗？”凌峰的声音有些发紧，他侧头看向妻子，发现她脸色苍白，握着自己的手指关节都泛了白。刚才那瞬间的强光和失重感太过诡异，像是被一只无形的大手猛地攥住，又狠狠抛了出去，现在脚踩在实地上，反倒有种不真切的漂浮感。
刘佳琪深吸一口气，摇了摇头：“没事，就是头有点晕……刚才那光到底是什么？是郎斯星人又回来了吗？”
半年前送别郎斯星人时，他们也曾见过类似的能量波动，只是那次温和得多，带着清晰的告别意味。可刚才的光，却透着一股蛮横的、不容抗拒的力量，像是时空被硬生生撕开了一道口子。
凌峰皱着眉没说话。他也不知道。郎斯星人临走时说过，短期内不会再到访，他们的文明有严格的星际公约，不会轻易干涉其他星球的时空秩序。可除了他们，还有谁能弄出这样的动静？
两人沉默着往下走，脚下的路渐渐从碎石变成了平整的水泥路，路边还多了一排太阳能路灯，造型简洁流畅，灯杆上嵌着的电子屏正滚动播放着一行绿色的字：“山林防火，人人有责——上海市应急管理局宣”。
“这路灯……”刘佳琪忽然停住脚步，指着那灯杆，“我记得上次来这边爬山，路灯还是普通的钠灯，没见过这种带屏幕的。”
凌峰也注意到了。不仅是路灯，远处山脚下隐约可见的公路上，行驶的汽车模样也透着古怪。它们的车身更低矮，线条更圆润，有些车顶还架着奇怪的金属杆，像是某种天线，而且行驶时几乎听不到发动机的轰鸣，安静得像滑行的幽灵。
“是有点不一样。”凌峰压下心头的疑虑，拉着她继续走，“可能是这半年翻新了设施吧，上海发展快，不奇怪。”
他想把这一切归结为正常的变化，可目光扫过远处的天际线时，心脏猛地一缩。
刚才在山顶被强光晃了眼，没来得及细看，此刻天色渐暗，远处的天空却亮得异常。不是晚霞，而是一种规整的、带着金属光泽的亮——十几艘造型奇特的飞行器正悬浮在半空，它们的轮廓像是拉长的水滴，表面覆盖着流动的蓝光，偶尔有一道光束从底部射向地面，在夜空中划出清晰的轨迹。
“那是……飞船？”刘佳琪的声音带着颤音。半年前他们见识过郎斯星人的飞船，可眼前这些，体积更大，形态更具压迫感，完全没有郎斯星飞船那种温和的流线型，反而透着一股冰冷的工业质感。
凌峰的喉咙有些发干。他从军时曾接触过不少前沿武器资料，可从未见过这样的飞行器能在城市上空如此从容地盘旋。这绝不是他熟悉的任何一个国家的科技水平，更不像是半年内可能实现的“发展”。
“先下山，找个地方问问情况。”凌峰定了定神，拉着刘佳琪加快了脚步。他有种强烈的预感，刚才那道白光，绝不仅仅是一次简单的能量爆发。
下山的路比记忆中短了不少，很快就走到了山脚下的停车场。这里停着不少车，大多是刚才看到的那种造型奇特的款式，还有几辆印着“森林消防”字样的车，车身上的标志是一个抽象的火焰图案，和他印象中红底黄焰的传统标志完全不同。
停车场旁有个小观景台，围着一圈栏杆，不少人正站在那里朝着远处的江面指指点点，议论声嗡嗡地飘过来。
“走，去看看。”凌峰拉着刘佳琪挤了过去。
观景台正对着黄浦江的入海口，此刻江面上的景象，让凌峰瞬间忘了呼吸。
夜色渐浓，江面上波光粼粼，可那些粼粼波光并非来自月光，而是来自三艘停泊在江心的巨大舰船。它们静卧在水面上，像三座黑色的岛屿，舰体上布满了不规则的凸起，有些地方闪烁着暗红色的光点，远远看去，像是蛰伏的巨兽睁开的眼睛。
这不是他认识的任何一种军舰。

凌峰曾在军港见过驱逐舰、护卫舰，甚至远远眺望过航母，那些舰船的轮廓方正硬朗，甲板上的炮管、雷达天线一目了然，透着阳刚的力量感。可眼前这三艘船，完全打破了他对“军舰”的所有认知。它们没有明显的甲板分层，舰体像是用一整块金属浇筑而成，表面覆盖着某种哑光的涂层，能吸收周围的光线，只有在偶尔转动的部位，才会露出内部复杂的机械结构。更诡异的是，它们周围的水面异常平静，连一丝涟漪都没有，仿佛被某种无形的力场隔绝开来。
“那是……咱们的军舰？”旁边有人发出疑问，声音里满是惊叹。
“应该是吧，昨天新闻里说，新型海防舰列装了，说是用了什么‘反重力缓冲系统’，停泊的时候能稳定周围水流，厉害吧？”另一个人语气自豪，拿出手里的“手机”对着江面拍照。那设备薄薄一片，像块透明的玻璃，屏幕亮起来时，能清晰地捕捉到远处舰船的细节。
凌峰的目光死死盯着那人手里的设备。这不是手机，至少不是他知道的手机。他口袋里还揣着自己的翻盖手机，是去年刚换的，在当时已经算时髦，可跟眼前这透明玻璃似的东西比起来，像是上个世纪的古董。
“反重力缓冲系统？”刘佳琪的声音在耳边响起，带着难以置信，“这……这是科幻电影里的东西吧？”
凌峰没回答，他的视线越过江面，落在更远处的岸边。那里有一片整齐的建筑群，风格简洁明快，高楼的外墙上覆盖着巨大的电子屏，正播放着城市夜景，画面清晰得像是身临其境。而在建筑群旁边的空地上，一队穿着制服的人正列队走过。
那是一支部队。
可他们的制服也透着古怪。不是他熟悉的橄榄绿或藏青，而是一种深灰色的紧身作战服，头盔上嵌着夜视仪，肩上背着的武器造型奇特，像是某种能量武器，而非传统的枪支。他们行走时步伐统一，动作利落，身上的装备在路灯下泛着冷光，整支队伍透着一股精密、肃杀的气息，和他记忆中部队那种带着烟火气的硬朗截然不同。
“佳琪，”凌峰的声音低得像耳语，指尖冰凉，“你看他们的臂章。”
刘佳琪顺着他的目光看去，只见那些人的左臂上，都戴着一个徽章——底色是鲜红的，上面印着五颗金色的五角星，排列方式和她熟悉的国徽一模一样。
是自己人。这个认知让她稍微松了口气，可紧随其后的，是更深的困惑。如果是自己人，为什么装备、服饰、连军舰都变得完全认不出来了？这半年里，到底发生了什么？
“凌峰，”她抓住丈夫的胳膊，声音发颤，“我们……是不是有什么地方不对劲？”
凌峰没有回答，只是紧紧握住她的手。他看着远处江面上那艘沉默的巨舰，它像一个巨大的问号，横亘在夜色里，无声地诉说着某种他无法理解的变化。空气中那丝若有若无的灼热感似乎又回来了，这次却带着一种冰冷的、陌生的气息。
他忽然想起刚才路灯上的电子屏，想起那行“上海市应急管理局宣”的字。一个荒谬却又挥之不去的念头，像冰冷的潮水般涌上心头：
他们脚下的这片土地，或许还是上海。
但他们所处的时间，已经不是那个送别郎斯星人后的、祥和安稳的半年。
那艘无言的军舰，那些沉默的士兵，还有这片既熟悉又陌生的夜空，都在无声地告诉他：你已经不在原来的世界了。
风从江面吹过来，带着江水的腥气，比山林里的风更冷，直透骨髓。凌峰下意识地将刘佳琪往怀里拉了拉，目光扫过周围那些对眼前景象习以为常的人们，第一次真切地感受到，自己成了这个“熟悉”世界里，最格格不入的异乡人。

Chapter 5: The Silent Warship
Ling Feng held Liu Jiaqi's arm, and the two of them walked slowly down the gravel road on the mountainside. The dazzling white light on the top of the mountain has disappeared, leaving only a vague burning sensation in the air, like the residual heat of a newly extinguished charcoal fire. The wind blew past my ears, carrying the scent of moist vegetation in the mountains and forests, but this familiar natural smell could not suppress the panic rising in my heart.
"Jiaqi, are you okay?" Ling Feng's voice was a little tight. He turned to look at his wife and found that her face was pale and the knuckles of her fingers turned white when she held him. The bright light and weightless feeling at that moment were too weird, as if I was suddenly grabbed by a big invisible hand and thrown away. Now that my feet are on the ground, I have an unreal feeling of floating.
Liu Jiaqi took a deep breath and shook her head: "It's okay, I'm just a little dizzy... What was that light just now? Is the Langsi star back again?"
They had seen similar energy fluctuations when they were bidding farewell to the Langsi people half a year ago, but that time it was much gentler and had a clear meaning of farewell. But the light just now revealed an overbearing and irresistible force, as if a hole had been torn open in time and space.
Ling Feng frowned and said nothing. He doesn't know either. Before leaving, the Langsi people said that they would not visit again in the short term. Their civilization has strict interstellar conventions and will not easily interfere with the time and space order of other planets. But besides them, who else could make such a noise?
The two of them walked down in silence. The road under their feet gradually changed from gravel to a smooth cement road. There was also a row of solar street lights on the roadside. The shape was simple and smooth. The electronic screen embedded in the light pole was scrolling and playing a line of green words: "Mountain forest fire prevention is everyone's responsibility - announced by the Shanghai Emergency Management Bureau."
"This street lamp..." Liu Jiaqi suddenly stopped and pointed to the lamp pole, "I remember the last time I came here to climb the mountain, the street lamps were ordinary sodium lamps. I have never seen one with a screen like this."
Ling Feng also noticed. Not only the street lights, but also the cars driving on the road looming at the foot of the mountain in the distance looked weird. Their bodies are lower and the lines are more rounded. Some of them have strange metal poles on the roof, like some kind of antenna. And when driving, you can barely hear the roar of the engine, and they are as quiet as a gliding ghost.
"It's a little different." Ling Feng suppressed the doubts in his heart and pulled her to continue walking, "Maybe it's because the facilities have been renovated in the past six months. Shanghai is developing rapidly, so it's not surprising."
He wanted to attribute all this to normal changes, but when his eyes swept across the distant skyline, his heart suddenly shrank.
I was dazzled by the bright light on the top of the mountain just now, and I didn't have time to take a closer look. At this moment, the sky was getting dark, but the sky in the distance was extremely bright. It's not sunset glow, but a regular, metallic glow - a dozen odd-shaped aircraft are suspended in mid-air. Their outlines are like elongated water droplets, and their surfaces are covered with flowing blue light. Occasionally, a beam of light shoots from the bottom to the ground, drawing a clear trajectory in the night sky.
"That's...a spaceship?" Liu Jiaqi's voice was trembling. They had seen the spacecraft of the Langs star half a year ago, but the ones in front of them were larger in size and more oppressive in shape. They did not have the gentle streamlined shape of the Langs star spacecraft, but had a cold industrial texture.
Ling Feng's throat was a little dry. He had been exposed to a lot of cutting-edge weapons information when he was in the army, but he had never seen such an aircraft hovering so calmly over the city. This was by no means the technological level of any country he was familiar with, let alone the "development" that could be achieved within half a year.
"Go down the mountain first and find a place to ask about the situation." Ling Feng calmed down and pulled Liu Jiaqi to speed up. He had a strong hunch that the white light just now was more than just a simple burst of energy.
The way down the mountain was much shorter than I remembered, and we soon reached the parking lot at the foot of the mountain. There were many cars parked here, most of them the strange-looking ones he saw just now, and there were also a few cars with the words "Forest Fire Fighting" printed on them. The logo on the car was an abstract flame pattern, which was completely different from the traditional logo of yellow flames on a red background in his impression.
There is a small viewing platform next to the parking lot, surrounded by a circle of railings. Many people are standing there pointing towards the river in the distance, and the sound of discussion floats over.
"Let's go take a look." Ling Feng pulled Liu Jiaqi and squeezed over.
The observation deck faces the estuary of the Huangpu River. The scene on the river at this moment made Ling Feng forget to breathe for a moment.
The night is getting darker, and there are sparkling waves on the river, but those sparkling waves do not come from the moonlight, but from three huge ships anchored in the center of the river. They lie quietly on the water, like three black islands. The hull is covered with irregular bulges, and some places are flashing with dark red light spots. From a distance, they look like the open eyes of a dormant giant beast.
This was not any kind of warship he knew.
Ling Feng had seen destroyers, frigates, and even aircraft carriers in the military port. The outlines of those ships were square and tough, and the gun barrels and radar antennas on the decks were clearly visible, exuding a sense of masculine power. But the three ships in front of him completely shattered all his understanding of "warships". They have no obvious deck layering. The hull seems to be cast from a single piece of metal. The surface is covered with some kind of matte coating, which can absorb the surrounding light. Only in occasional rotations will the complex internal mechanical structure be exposed. What's even weirder is that the water around them is extremely calm, without even a ripple, as if they are isolated by some invisible force field.
"That's... our warship?" Someone next to him asked, his voice full of exclamation.
"It should be so. Yesterday, the news said that a new type of coastal defense ship has been installed. It said that it uses an 'anti-gravity buffer system' to stabilize the surrounding water flow when it is anchored. Isn't it amazing?" Another person sounded proud and took out his "mobile phone" to take pictures of the river. The device is as thin as a piece of transparent glass. When the screen lights up, it can clearly capture the details of the distant ship.
Ling Feng's eyes were fixed on the device in the man's hand. It wasn't a cell phone, at least not one he knew. He also carried his own flip phone in his pocket, which he had just replaced last year. It was considered fashionable at the time, but compared with the transparent glass-like thing in front of him, it looked like an antique from the last century.
"Anti-gravity buffer system?" Liu Jiaqi's voice sounded in her ears, with disbelief, "This...is this something from a science fiction movie, right?"
Ling Feng didn't answer. His eyes crossed the river and landed on the shore farther away. There is a neat group of buildings with a simple and bright style. The outer walls of the tall buildings are covered with huge electronic screens, which are playing the night view of the city. The picture is so clear that it feels like you are actually there. In the open space next to the building complex, a group of uniformed people were walking past in formation.
That's an army.
But their uniforms are also weird. It was not the olive green or navy blue that he was familiar with, but a dark gray tight-fitting combat uniform with a night vision device embedded in the helmet and a strange-looking weapon on his shoulder, like some kind of energy weapon rather than a traditional gun. They walked with uniform steps and neat movements. Their equipment glowed coldly under the street lights. The whole team exuded a precise and chilling atmosphere, which was completely different from the pyrotechnic toughness of the troops in his memory.
"Jia Qi," Ling Feng's voice was as low as a whisper, his fingertips were cold, "Look at their armbands."
Liu Jiaqi followed his gaze and saw that those people were wearing a badge on their left arms - the background color was bright red, with five golden five-pointed stars printed on it, arranged in the same way as the national emblem she was familiar with.
It's one of our own. This realization made her feel slightly relieved, but what followed was a deeper confusion. If it was one of our own, why were the equipment, clothing, and even the warships completely unrecognizable? What happened in the past six months?
"Ling Feng," she grabbed her husband's arm, her voice trembling, "Is there something wrong with us...?"
Ling Feng didn't answer, just held her hand tightly. He looked at the silent giant ship on the river in the distance. It was like a huge question mark, stretching across the night, silently telling some changes that he could not understand. The vague burning sensation in the air seemed to be back again, this time with a cold, unfamiliar breath.
He suddenly remembered the electronic screen on the street lamp just now, and the words "Shanghai Emergency Management Bureau Announcement". A ridiculous but lingering thought came to my mind like a cold tide:
The land beneath their feet may still be Shanghai.
But the time they lived in was no longer the peaceful and stable half a year after bidding farewell to Lang Si.
The silent warship, those silent soldiers, and the familiar yet unfamiliar night sky all silently told him: You are no longer in the original world.
The wind blows from the river, carrying the fishy smell of the river. It is colder than the wind in the mountains and forests, and penetrates to the bone marrow. Ling Feng subconsciously pulled Liu Jiaqi into his arms and glanced at the people around him who were accustomed to the scene in front of them. For the first time, he truly felt that he had become the most out of place stranger in this "familiar" world.
